what.text: At the end of 2025, UNHCR reported 9139309 people displaced inside Sudan by conflict whom UNHCR protects or assists.
Refugees from Sudan live in top host countries including Chad, South Sudan, Libya, Ethiopia, and Uganda.
By the end of 2025, Chad hosted 1330950 refugees from Sudan.

why.text: In 2003, the War in Darfur began as armed groups in Darfur, including JEM and SLM/A, fought the government.

Sudan experienced the Armed conflict over the government of Sudan, which was active from 1998 to 2018 with opposition groups NDA, SPLM/A, JEM, SLM/A, NRF, SLM/A - MM, SLFA, SSDM/A, SPLM/A-North, SRF, SSLM/A, Darfur Joint Resistance Forces, and SARC, and from 2020 to 2025 with opposition groups SLM/A, RSF, SPLM/A-North, and SFA.
In April 2023, fighting broke out during the War between the army and the RSF between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF).
The disaster hazards recorded for internal displacement in Sudan are Flood and Mass Movement.

when.text: On 9 July 2011, South Sudan became independent and separated from Sudan, creating a series break because figures for Sudan before and after 2011 cover different territory.
After the War between the army and the RSF broke out in April 2023, IDMC recorded 6038666 new internal displacements inside Sudan from conflict and violence during 2023.
During the main displacement years of 2023 to 2025, the number of people living in internal displacement inside Sudan because of conflict and violence reached 9116896 at the end of 2025.

how.text: The sources do not state the routes that displaced people take.
UNHCR counts people displaced inside Sudan by conflict whom UNHCR protects or assists as year-end totals.
IDMC counts new internal displacements as movements during each year rather than individual people, meaning one person can be displaced more than once.
